uscode.house.gov.notes: Straight U+0022 double quotes around amended text. Vulgar fraction U+00BD set tight: "age 59½". U+2013 appears only inside Pub. L. numbers, never as a structural dash.

www.govinfo.gov.notes: Straight double quotes. Statutory dash is a tight em dash: "paragraph (1)—(A)". Embeds <!-- PDFPage:NNNN --> comments *inside* words, so tag stripping must not insert a space.

www.law.cornell.edu.notes: Curly U+201C/U+201D double quotes around defined terms. Some CFR pages use the U+2044 fraction slash ("70 1⁄2"). LII CFR pages carry far less text than the eCFR original — prefer eCFR for regulations.

www.ecfr.gov.notes: Renders halves as "70 1⁄2" with U+2044 and surrounding spaces. Straight double quotes.

www.irs.gov.notes: Inconsistent between publications: P969 and i5329 use U+2019, P590-B uses U+0027. Contractions ("doesn’t", "can’t") are the publication's own voice and must be quoted as written. PDFs on this host lose every one of these characters in extraction — see PDF handling.
